text:
tara: heads-up — our unit tests started failing in CI after the sdk ESM switch. error in the matrix job (node:20) says: SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export' in /home/runner/work/repo/dist/cjs/auth.js

eli: that sounds like something requiring an ESM file as CJS or vice-versa. do you have transformIgnorePatterns in Jest? often node_modules/ gets skipped and our dual-published package ends up untransformed.

tara: Jest config (snippet):
```
module.exports = {
  preset: 'ts-jest',
  testEnvironment: 'node',
  transformIgnorePatterns: ['/node_modules/'],
}
```

cheng: hmm. ts-jest has an ESM mode. if your package is ESM-first we set `globals: { 'ts-jest': { useESM: true } }` and `extensionsToTreatAsEsm: ['.ts']`. Also set `transformIgnorePatterns` to exclude our sdk: `transformIgnorePatterns: ['/node_modules/(?!redwood-sdk)']`.

tara: we do that for jest but the failing job is Vitest on another matrix axis. Vitest errors with `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` when some helper tries to require('redwood-sdk/auth').

eli: vitest's resolver (vite) respects package.json exports more strictly than node sometimes. In your vitest.config.ts try: `resolve: { conditions: ['import', 'node'] }` and `deps: { inline: ['redwood-sdk'] }` so the test runner bundles the ESM.

cheng: also check that you don't alias the package to src/ during local dev; that can mask issues. If you alias to `src` for DX, CI will still pull from dist. If your helpers still use `require()` they will force CJS resolution. Convert helpers to `import` if possible.

tara: interesting — we have a legacy test helper that does `const {setup} = require('./test-utils')` and that file does `const sdk = require('redwood-sdk')`. will migrate.

eli: for mocks: prefer asynchronous ESM-friendly patterns. Example for vitest: `vi.mock('redwood-sdk/auth', async () => { const actual = await vi.importActual('redwood-sdk/auth'); return { ...actual, getToken: vi.fn(() => 'fake') } })`. For jest (CJS) you can keep `jest.mock` but ensure ts-jest/Babel transpiles the import path.

cheng: another gotcha — transform order. If you use babel-jest + ts-jest the module syntax can flip. Try single transformer strategy (ts-jest in ESM mode usually works). For babel, enable `sourceType: 'unambiguous'` only as a last resort.

tara: CI still flaky — sometimes tests pass on node 18 but fail node 20. Is that expected?

eli: yes, resolver heuristics changed across Node versions and Vite/Vitest dependencies. Add a CI matrix to run node 18/20 locally to reproduce. Also ensure your Docker runner is actually using the declared version (some GH actions images have multiple node versions cached).

cheng: long-term: add a small `test-resolution` script that prints `require.resolve('redwood-sdk/auth')` and `await import('redwood-sdk/auth')` output in both runners. That narrows whether package.exports conditions are chosen.

ci-bot: Workflow: unit-tests (ubuntu-latest, node: 20.x) — job queued.

tara: plan: 1) convert test helpers to ESM where easy; 2) tighten vitest.resolve.conditions and deps.inline for sdk; 3) tune jest ts-jest useESM + extensionsToTreatAsEsm; 4) add transformIgnorePatterns exception for redwood-sdk; 5) add node 18/20 CI matrix.

eli: if you want I can draft the ts-jest + vitest snippets and a tiny script to debug resolver behavior.

tara: please — would save a lot. thanks! :raised_hands:

devx-bot: Note: file an SDK issue if changing transforms is not feasible for downstream users — we may add a small `cjs-bridge` at publish time.

tara: good call. adding issue for `cjs-bridge` re-export shim. tl;dr: mixed ESM/CJS + transform settings + legacy require helpers = flaky CI. fixing helpers + resolver config should stabilize tests.
